Work with Us. Change the World.

We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.
We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.
Job Description
We’re looking for a developing civil engineer to support the delivery of site infrastructure design packages across a range of projects. You’ll contribute to stormwater, earthworks and basic water/wastewater designs, coordinate with other disciplines, and build strong technical fundamentals under the guidance of senior engineers.
What you’ll be doing
- Perform specific and limited portions of broader civil/site infrastructure assignments under moderate supervision, to agreed budget and programme.

- Work on detailed or routine design tasks involving calculations, modelling and relatively simple tests/checks.
- Support delivery of key infrastructure elements, including:- Stormwater design (pit and pipe layouts, hydraulic checks, minor drainage design)
- Bulk earthworks support (grading plans, levels coordination, basic cut/fill inputs)
- Basic water and wastewater infrastructure (reticulation layouts, tie-ins, design checks)
- WSUD support where required (e.g., contributing to concept layouts and design documentation).
- Propose practical approaches to new problems, escalating early where needed and applying learnings from previous tasks.
- Identify discrepancies in calculations, drawings, models or inputs and raise them promptly for resolution.
- Coordinate with internal disciplines and external stakeholders on interfaces (services coordination, site constraints, constructability).
- Provide day-to-day support and informal guidance to graduates/entry-level engineers (as appropriate).
Qualifications

- 2–5 years’ post-graduate experience in civil/site infrastructure design.

Site Engineer – Civil Construction & Earthworks
Location: Sydney, NSW | Remote Travel Required
Salary: $120,000 – $145,000 + Superannuation
Employment Type: Full-Time | Permanent
About Us
Sydney Earthworks is a civil construction and earthworks company delivering projects across Sydney and regional NSW. We specialise in bulk earthworks, excavation, site preparation and civil infrastructure works.
With a growing pipeline of projects, we are seeking an experienced and motivated Site Engineer to join our team.
This role is primarily based in Sydney; however, applicants must be willing and available to travel to regional and remote project locations as required.
About the Role
As a Site Engineer, you will be responsible for coordinating and overseeing site engineering activities, ensuring projects are delivered safely, efficiently, on schedule and in accordance with project specifications.
You will work closely with Project Managers, Site Supervisors, subcontractors and clients to support the successful delivery of civil construction and earthworks projects.
Key Responsibilities
- Coordinate and manage day-to-day engineering activities across civil construction sites.
- Interpret construction drawings, specifications and technical documentation.
- Monitor project progress, budgets, schedules and productivity.
- Assist with project planning, programming and resource allocation.
- Manage quality assurance documentation, inspections, ITPs and compliance records.
- Coordinate subcontractors, suppliers, plant and site personnel.
- Undertake site measurements, quantity calculations and progress reporting.
- Assist with procurement, variations, claims and cost tracking.
- Ensure construction activities comply with WHS requirements, relevant standards and project specifications.
- Liaise with clients, consultants, surveyors and project stakeholders.
- Identify and resolve technical and operational issues on site.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will have:
- A Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering or a related discipline.
- Minimum 3 years' experience in a Site Engineer role within civil construction.
- Demonstrated experience in bulk earthworks, excavation, civil infrastructure or similar projects.
- Strong understanding of construction methodologies, drawings and specifications.
- Experience with quality assurance, project reporting and cost control.
- Excellent communication, organisational and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work independently and effectively within a project team.
- Strong knowledge of Australian construction standards and WHS requirements.
- A current Australian driver's licence.
- A valid White Card.
- Willingness and availability to travel and work at regional or remote project locations when required.
What We Offer
- Competitive salary of $120,000 – $145,000 + Superannuation, depending on experience.
- Permanent, full-time employment.
- Opportunity to work on diverse civil construction and earthworks projects.
- Exposure to both metropolitan and regional projects.
- Supportive and experienced management team.
- Career development opportunities within a growing company.
How to Apply
If you are a driven Site Engineer looking to take the next step in your career, we would love to hear from you.
Applicants must have full Australian working rights and be available for travel to regional and remote project locations as required.

Recent and current projects include:

•      Fremantle Bridge, Swan River Crossing (WA) - permanent formwork for the new river crossing
•      North East Link (VIC) - formwork supplied across various sections of Melbourne’s major motorway project
See more of our work at Permadec Projects and on LinkedIn.
THE ROLE
We are looking for an experienced drafter to take on design and drafting for our Australian and New Zealand projects. You will produce panel layouts and quantity take-offs, work closely with our experienced UK design team, and support sales, estimating and project delivery with accurate, buildable drawings. ·        Work with the UK design team on design, detailing and drawing standards
·        Prepare drawing packages and submittals for contractors and their engineers
·        Support sales, estimating and project managers from tender through to delivery
WHAT YOU’LL BRING
·        Solid drafting experience (typically 3+ years) in formwork and/or civil infrastructure - bridges, rail, marine or similar
·        Strong AutoCAD 2D skills
·        Experience with quantity take-offs
·        Self-motivated and organised - able to manage your own workload remotely and communicate clearly online
·        Relevant drafting qualification (e.g. Certificate IV or Diploma in engineering drafting) or equivalent experience
·        Strong Microsoft office capabilities – particularly in Microsoft Excel
·        Right to work in Australia
DESIRABLE
·        Allplan or other 3D modelling experience
·        Experience with precast or permanent formwork systems
·        Interest in growing into a lead role
WHAT WE OFFER
·        Fully remote role
·        Work on major infrastructure projects across Australia and NZ, as part of an international group
·        Mentoring from an experienced international design team
·        Real career progression toward leading the Australian design function
·        Competitive salary plus super, matched to experience
HOW TO APPLY
Email your CV and a short cover note outlining your drafting experience to sales@permadec.com.au, with “Design Drafter application” in the subject line.
Drawing samples are welcome. Applications are reviewed as they are received.
Permadec is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified people.

A cadetship with Council offers the opportunity to combine tertiary study with valuable industry experience while contributing to projects that support our local area.

All applications must include;

About us
PD Project Delivery (PDPD) is a Brisbane civil engineering consultancy. We support clients with project management, engineering and supervision on major infrastructure projects across Queensland, from data centres and rail to energy and civil works. Our small head office team supports our people on site, so you can get on with the job.
About the opportunity
We're looking for Civil Engineers to join a large-scale data centre project in Queensland.
Data centres are the infrastructure behind cloud computing and AI, and they're being built quickly. This is your chance to put a high-profile, technically demanding project on your CV and work with a strong site team from the early stages of the build.
The point of hire is Brisbane. The role is bus-in/bus-out on a 15 days on, 6 days off roster.
What you'll be doing
•         Delivering civil works on site, including earthworks, drainage, roads, pavements and underground services
•         Supervising subcontractors and making sure work is built to drawings and specifications
•         Managing quality: ITPs, lot records, test results and conformance reporting
•         Coordinating set-out and survey, and checking as-built information
•         Raising and tracking RFIs, NCRs and variations
•         Contributing to programming and progress reporting
•         Promoting and maintaining a strong safety culture on site
What we're looking for
•         Degree in Civil Engineering (or equivalent)
•         3 years' hands-on, site-based experience on civil construction or infrastructure projects
•         Solid working knowledge of earthworks, drainage and services
•         Experience with QA documentation and lot management
•         Construction Induction (White Card) and a current driver's licence
•         Full Australian working rights
•         Happy to work a BIBO 15/6 roster from a Brisbane point of hire
What's in it for you
•         A major data centre project on your CV
•         6 days at home every swing
•         Travel from Brisbane to site organised for you
•         Ongoing work with PD after this project. We support clients on projects across Queensland, so finishing this job doesn't mean you're out of work.
•         A team that looks after its people and backs your career development

Click Apply and attach your resume.

candidates.content_text:
About the role
Negri Contractors is seeking an experienced Civil Construction Site Engineers to join our team across Melbourne. This is a full-time position that plays a crucial role in the successful delivery of our civil construction projects. As a Site Engineer, you will be responsible for on-site coordination, quality assurance, and technical oversight of construction activities. This role is essential to ensuring projects are completed on time, within budget, and to the highest standards of safety and quality. You will work on-site at our metro locations, collaborating closely with project management, contractors, and site teams to drive project success.
What you'll be doing
- Coordinating daily construction activities and liaising between design teams, contractors, and subcontractors on-site
- Conducting regular site inspections and quality assurance checks to ensure compliance with design specifications and industry standards
- Monitoring site safety protocols and ensuring adherence to all relevant health and safety legislation and company policies
- Preparing and maintaining site records, including daily reports, progress documentation, and as-built drawings
- Managing site logistics, including material delivery coordination, equipment allocation, and site layout planning
- Identifying and resolving technical issues and engineering challenges that arise during construction
- Communicating progress updates to project management and stakeholders on schedule and budget performance
- Assisting in budget tracking and cost control measures throughout the construction phase
- Supporting the project team in meeting contractual obligations and regulatory requirements
What we're looking for
- Tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering or a related engineering discipline
- 3–5 years of post-graduation experience working as a Site Engineer on civil construction projects
- Strong knowledge of civil construction methods, materials, and best practices
- Proficiency in reading and interpreting construction drawings, specifications, and technical documentation
- Experience with site management software and digital tools for documentation and reporting
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively with diverse teams
- Sound understanding of health and safety regulations, including site-specific risk management
- Strong attention to detail and organisational skills to manage multiple tasks and documentation
- Problem-solving abilities and the capacity to work independently and make technical decisions under pressure
- A valid driver's licence and willingness to travel between project sites as required
- Preferred: Experience with specific construction specialisations such as roads, bridges, drainage, or structural works
What we offer

About Us
Located 35km to the southeast of Melbourne, Greater
Dandenong City Council covers 129 square kilometres and has a population of
over 169,000 people. The central activities district is Melbourne's second
largest retail and commercial centre and includes large shopping complexes at
Dandenong and Keysborough as well as the highly popular Dandenong Market.
Greater Dandenong City Council is the most culturally
diverse locality in Australia, with residents from over 150 different
birthplaces, nearly two-thirds of whom were born overseas. Key industries
include manufacturing, health care and social assistance, retail trade,
wholesale trade and transport.
We are a progressive organisation of exceptional character
that offers a dynamic and rewarding work environment to approximately 900
employees. We recognise that our staff are vital to the delivery of excellent
service to our community and the achievement of our long-term vision. We invest
in the development of our people, and we strive to be a workplace that is
respectful, engaged, accountable, creative and honest.
About
the role
This is an
excellent opportunity for a civil engineer who wants to build experience across
infrastructure planning, drainage, asset planning, capital works development
and strategic infrastructure projects. You'll help shape the future of Greater
Dandenong's infrastructure network by investigating complex engineering issues,
developing practical and sustainable solutions, and preparing projects for
delivery through Council's Capital Works Program. Working closely with internal
stakeholders, external authorities and the community, you'll contribute to
infrastructure outcomes that support growth, service delivery, resilience and
long-term asset sustainability.
From planning through to project
development, you'll gain experience across Strategic
infrastructure planning, Drainage and
flood risk management, Development
facilitation, Capital works
prioritisation, Business case and
scope development, External funding
opportunities, Stakeholder
engagement and collaboration with organisations such as Melbourne Water, the
Department of Transport and Planning, utility providers and major
infrastructure authorities.
Whether your background is in civil
engineering, drainage, asset management or infrastructure planning, you'll have
the opportunity to broaden your skills while working on diverse projects that
make a real difference to the community.
About
you
You're
a motivated and solutions-focused civil engineer who enjoys tackling complex
infrastructure challenges and developing practical outcomes that benefit the
community. You have a strong understanding of civil infrastructure planning,
drainage, asset management or infrastructure strategy, and are comfortable
working with a wide range of stakeholders to influence and support
decision-making. You are analytical, proactive and able to balance technical,
financial and community considerations when developing infrastructure
solutions. You will have:
- A degree qualification in Civil
Engineering or a related discipline.
- Experience in infrastructure planning,
drainage, asset management, civil engineering or a related field.
- Experience analysing infrastructure
issues and developing practical, evidence-based solutions.
- Knowledge of relevant legislation,
standards, guidelines and codes of practice relating to civil infrastructure
and local government.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving and
decision-making skills.

communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear technical advice
and reports, business cases and recommendations.

internal and external stakeholders to achieve positive project and service
outcomes.

multidisciplinary team.

development.

or other government agencies.
- Experience preparing funding
applications, business cases or long-term infrastructure plans.
- Membership of Engineers Australia or
eligibility for membership.

candidates.content_text:
Seeking:
 Civil Project Engineer x 1 (5+ years’ field experience)
 Civil Site Engineer x 1 (2+ years’ post-grad experience)
 For various projects across the Pacific Islands
Small-ish local civil works, marine infrastructure and coastal remediation.
 Character building setting. Remote. Isolated. Logistically difficult.
 The commute in and out is long and clunky, which is why the roster is set at 4 weeks on, 2 weeks off (6-day working week, Sundays off).
Flights, travel, visas, meals and accommodation provided.
A long way from anywhere. Not the kind of place you can pack up your bat and ball and head home at a moment’s notice.
You’ll need to be level-headed. Reliable. Consistent in how you show up, day in, day out. The kind of person who can be counted on.
Capacity to work as part of a team is a critical quality on this gig.
 You’ll also need to be able to cope with temporary camp conditions in a hot, humid, tropical setting.
The Reward?
 Yes, the money is good.
 Feel good factor also high.
 A real sense of accomplishment, knowing your individual effort is contributing to capacity building in developing nations.
 Projects that matter, for communities that need them.
Must Haves
 If your pointy finger is hovering over the “Apply Now” button: Terrific.
 But before you click, please double check this MUST HAVE list:
 - Tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering or Construction Management
 - In-field project experience (marine, coastal or structures highly regarded)
 - Sound technical ability
 - People skills: it’s isolated, and you’ll get lonely and a bit snarky from time to time. So it’s mission critical you can work well with others, and that you’re not the one who gets on everyone’s nerves
 - Australian citizenship or permanent residency status. This is a non-negotiable part of the contract; eligibility for PR, or a visa permitting work in Australia, will NOT be sufficient (sorry)
 - A current passport
 - Partner Clearance: i.e. you’ve already discussed this as a possibility with your loved one, rather than getting all the way through the process before landing it on them
 This gig is tough. No point pretending otherwise.
 But it’s the kind of tough that might just satisfy your sense of adventure. It also comes with a seriously high feel good factor.
If that sounds like your kind of ride, don’t overthink it.
 Giddy up and get going.

bullets: Work on significant transport infrastructure projects across Queensland

candidates.content_text:
Bring your curiosity and determination to make a positive impact on the future of transport, and we’ll help you go all the way.
GHD’s Construction Phase Services group in Queensland has been providing contract administration, construction management and independent assurance services to government and private clients for over 30 years. Our team has contributed to major transport infrastructure projects including the Kangaroo Point Green Bridge, Bruce Highway Cooroy to Curra and M1 Burleigh to Palm Beach.
We are currently seeking experienced Site Engineers with bridges, road works, rail and/or general infrastructure experience to join our projects in both metro and regional areas of Queensland.  
This is a rare opportunity for ambitious Site Engineers to join an industry leader in contract administration and become part of a high-performing team delivering some of Queensland’s most significant infrastructure projects.
Working alongside respected industry professionals, you’ll have access to advanced contract management systems, proven delivery frameworks and the support of a collaborative team passionate about excellence.
If you're looking to accelerate your career, broaden your experience and help shape the future of critical infrastructure, we want to hear from you.
Working with an energetic and high-performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:
•    Supporting Senior Project Engineers and the Administrator’s Representative with contract administration, management and project reporting.
•    Preparing monthly quantity forecasts and estimates in collaboration with the broader engineering team.
•    Supporting project risk management, including updates to the risk register, forecast final costs and required contingency.
•    Assisting with the preparation of monthly reporting to TMR.
•    Working closely with Engineers and Inspectors to ensure accurate field records and agreed measurements are available to support the assessment of progress claims, variations and extension of time claims.
•    Assisting the Administrator’s Representative with the assessment and validation of cost and time claims.
•    Coordinating with the Project Planning Engineer on program updates and assessments of progress and delays.
•    Assessing monthly progress claims and preparing payment certificates for approval.
•    Supporting Senior Project Engineers in reviewing and verifying management plans, construction methodologies, programs, variations, progress claims and quality records.
•    Supporting audit and reporting processes across traffic, environmental, risk and safety management.
•    Maintaining relevant contract administration systems and project records.
•    Participating in project meetings and preparing and issuing minutes as required.
•    Building strong working relationships with the client, contractors and wider project team.
•    Working collaboratively with clients, the GHD team and contractors to identify and resolve issues, helping keep projects on track.
•    Supporting the Contract Administration team to ensure GHD meets its obligations under the contract.
What you will bring to the team
We’re looking for motivated engineers who want to build their experience in major infrastructure delivery and develop strong contract administration and commercial capability.
•    A Bachelor of Engineering in Civil or Structural Engineering.
•    Membership of Engineers Australia and Registered Professional Engineer of Queensland (RPEQ) preferred, or an equivalent professional accreditation (e.g. CPEng), or the ability to obtain these credentials. 
•    A minimum of 5 years’ experience within the construction industry.
•    Previous experience working with TMR specifications and general conditions of contract.
•    Strong interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills.
•    The ability to work effectively within a collaborative, high-performing project team.
•    Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
Previous experience in the commercial management of infrastructure projects will be highly regarded, as will TMR prequalification at SEC01 or SEC02 level.
Build your career with GHD
This is more than an opportunity to work on one major project.  As a permanent member of GHD’s Construction Phase Services team, you’ll have the opportunity to develop your capability in contract administration and major infrastructure delivery while learning from experienced industry professionals.
It’s an opportunity to broaden your technical and commercial experience, build strong client and industry relationships, and establish a longer-term career delivering complex transport infrastructure projects with GHD.
Interested?  Apply Online.
GHD is an equal opportunity employer, and we want everyone to be able to fully participate in our recruitment process. We value a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and people of all identities.
GHD embraces a range of flexible work practices to create a work environment focused on well-being, flexibility and productivity where our people can thrive.
We respectfully ask that no agency resumes be presented at this stage.

We are expanding our drafting capability in our Victoria / Queensland offices. UDEC is seeking an experienced Civil Engineering Draftsperson (Drafter) to produce construction-ready documentation for major infrastructure projects across Australia. The Drafter role forms part of the Drafting team and assists in transforming engineering concepts into precise technical drawings whilst achieving quality documentation. The Drafter is responsible for assisting Civil Engineering Professionals with drawing production on projects, and contributing to continuous improvement of company CAD systems
This is a full-time position with UDEC based in our UDEC office, reporting to the CADD Manager National.
UDEC is looking for a highly motivated individual with a keen interest in developing and broadening their skills and experience in the Public Utilities, Water and Wastewater Industry within an engineering company with a primary focus on major infrastructure projects across Australia.
Duties and Responsibilities:
- Effective utilisation of computer-aided design and drafting software applications applicable to utility infrastructure design
- Assist in undertaking various planning and design activities for utility projects to achieve successful completion within time, quality, cost and stakeholder expectations
- Coordinate design with other disciplines
- Identify project scope and programme requirements to carry out the work, specific to each job being undertaken
- Develop and produce technical drawings as required by the Project Manager, Engineers, Designers using CAD, digital graphics and desktop publishing computer systems
- Undertake engineering modelling and drafting works
- Identify requirements to carry out the work
- Ongoing continual professional development and familiarity with relevant codes, regulations and industry standards
- Adherence to UDEC Quality Management System project requirements including CAD requirements
What We Look For:
Experience
- 2+ years of relevant experience in preparing drawings for civil infrastructure projects using 2D drafting software within an Australian Consultancy
Software skills
- Proficient in AutoCAD (2D production and sheet set management)
- Proficient in the use of Synergy
- Software customisation, script authoring, etc.
Qualifications
- Tertiary education in relevant discipline 
Technical Knowledge
- Strong understanding of CAD standards, civil drafting conventions, standard symbols and presentation guidelines across various Australian states
- Solid working knowledge of relevant Australian Standards and State Government drafting requirements
Delivery
- Ability to prioritise and prepare drawings for civil infrastructure projects and deliver to deadlines
Communication
- Excellent verbal and written skills
- Skilled at collaborative working, have good interpersonal skills and an ability to communicate effectively
Additional features of the role (travel or physical requirements): 
- Generally based at UDEC Melbourne or Brisbane office but may be required to work from dedicated Major Projects offices as required for project delivery.
Our People:
Our people are our number one asset, and we are committed to providing a workplace that supports our team to grow.
UDEC personnel have worked together to build an industry reputation as a cohesive, experienced and effective team, valued for their contribution in delivering successful projects to our clients and ensure that there is no compromise on the quality we deliver.
What We Offer:
- A genuine career role for an experienced and enthusiastic Drafter looking to continue to develop their professional experience within the major infrastructure project environment;
- Clear career progression paths into design management or principal technical roles;
- Opportunity to work across a diverse range of challenging projects;
- Flexible working arrangements will be considered by mutual agreement and according to operational requirements;
- An attractive remuneration package commensurate with experience;
- Vibrant team culture with a dynamic and highly skilled team;
- Strong organisational values with a work/life balance; and
- Employee opportunities, training and career progression.
UDEC is committed to Equal Employment Opportunities and invites applications from people of all nationalities, genders, and cultural backgrounds, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders.

To learn more about what we do, go to: http://www.udec.com.au/ 
If you are interested in becoming part of the UDEC team and believe you meet the criteria, apply via email to: recruitment@udec.com.au
Applications close Friday 20 November 2026 at 5pm (AEDT).
Your application should include a Covering Letter addressing how you meet the above criteria and your Resume outlining your experience.

- Read reinforcement/steel schedules and coordinate bar marks, reinforcement sizes, quantities, bends, laps, couplers and placement requirements with the site team.
- Prepare material take-offs and complete order forms for reinforcement, formwork, concrete and associated consumables; check quantities, lead times and delivery requirements.
- Coordinate deliveries, storage and availability of materials to suit the construction programme and avoid delays or unnecessary wastage.
- Assist with planning and sequencing formwork, reinforcement, pre-pour inspections, concrete placement, finishing and curing activities.
- Check set-out, dimensions, levels, formwork alignment, reinforcement placement, concrete cover, cast-in items, penetrations and embeds against approved drawings.
- Arrange and coordinate inspections and ensure required hold points are released before work proceeds or concrete is poured.
- Maintain current drawings on site and raise requests for information (RFIs) where drawings, schedules or site conditions are unclear or inconsistent.
- Coordinate site crews, subcontractors, suppliers and plant to ensure work is completed safely, efficiently and to the required quality.
- Monitor daily progress, quantities and productivity against the programme; identify constraints and report delays or potential impacts to the Project Manager.
- Prepare short-term and look-ahead programmes and coordinate upcoming labour, materials, equipment and inspection requirements.
- Maintain site records, daily reports, delivery dockets, checklists, inspection records, concrete pour records and other project documentation.
- Ensure works comply with approved drawings, project specifications, ITPs, quality requirements, WHS legislation and company procedures.
- Identify defects, non-conformances and rework risks; assist with corrective actions and close-out documentation.
- Record variations and additional works, maintain supporting quantity records and provide information for progress claims and cost tracking.
- Liaise with the Project Manager and procurement team regarding material orders, supplier issues, costs, substitutions and programme requirements.
- Provide technical support to supervisors and crews and help resolve construction issues in consultation with the Project Manager.
- Promote safe work practices, good housekeeping and coordination between work groups, particularly during lifting, reinforcement installation and concrete pours.
- Collaborate with management and the wider project team to improve construction methods, reduce waste and achieve project outcomes.

- Tertiary Engineering Qualifications and/or relevant construction experience
- WHS Construction Induction
- Minimum 2-3 years’ experience in a project delivery-based role
- Demonstrated competency in project management
- Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, FRP drawings, sections, details and specifications
- Ability to read reinforcement / steel schedules and identify bar marks, sizes, quantities, laps, bends and placement requirements
- Ability to measure and quantify formwork, reinforcement and concrete requirements from drawings
- Ability to prepare material take-offs and complete purchase / order forms for formwork, reinforcement, concrete and associated materials
- Understanding of formwork systems, reinforcement installation, concrete placement and curing requirements
- Ability to check set-out, dimensions, levels, cover, embedments, cast-ins and penetrations against approved drawings
- Knowledge of inspection and test plans (ITPs), hold points, checklists and quality records
- Understanding of construction sequencing, short-term planning and look-ahead programmes
- Commercial awareness, including tracking quantities, wastage, variations and progress
- Effective problem-solving, time-management and organisational skills
- Clear written and verbal communication and effective coordination with supervisors, crews, subcontractors, suppliers and the Project Manager

At Bayside Council, we are committed to a positive, flexible and supportive workplace culture, where our people and customers feel respected and valued. We are proud to serve our community through operating with transparency, integrity and in the best interests of the Bayside community to deliver exceptional service.
About the role
Bayside Council is seeking an experienced and motivated Stormwater and Floodplain Engineer to play a key role in managing Councils stormwater infrastructure, reducing flood risk and delivering sustainable outcomes for our community.
The divers and rewarding role offer the opportunity to contribute to strategic infrastructure planning, floodplain risk management, stormwater asset management and the delivery of capital works and flood mitigation initiatives. You will provide specialist technical advice, manage complex projects and help shape resilient and sustainable infrastructure across Bayside.
Primary purpose of the role is to:
- Provide expert technical advice on stormwater-related issues to internal and external stakeholders.
- Lead and coordinate flood studies, floodplain risk management studies and plans and flood mitigation strategies in accordance with the NSW Flood Risk Management Framework.
- Develop and implement policies for managing flood-prone land within Bayside LGA to mitigate risk.
- Plan and deliver sustainable stormwater capital works programs that meet service levels and community needs while minimising asset lifecycle costs.
- Coordinate contractors and consultants for planning, construction, and maintenance of drainage systems, stormwater treatment measures, and flood mitigation works.
- Prepare project briefs for capital works, flood studies, and risk management plans.

For further details about the position and its responsibilities, please refer to the Position Description.
About you
To succeed in this role, you will be proactive and technically capable engineer with demonstrated experience in stormwater engineering, floodplain risk management and infrastructure planning. You will possess strong analytical and problem-solving skills, sound engineering judgement and the ability to develop practical and sustainable solutions to complex engineer challenges.
You will bring:
- A degree in Civil Engineering or an equivalent qualification that meets the eligibility requirements for membership with Engineers Australia.
- Demonstrated experience in urban stormwater drainage, catchment management, floodplain risk management and stormwater infrastructure planning.
- Sound knowledge of the NSW Flood Risk Management Framework, floodplain risk management processes and stormwater asset management principles.
- Strong technical skills, including proficiency in hydrological and hydraulic modelling software, databases, and data analysis tools.
- Ability to interpret technical investigations, assess development proposals and provide clear, practical engineering advice.
- Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement skills.

The Cressbrook Dam Safety Improvement Project is a major dam safety and flood resilience upgrade delivering complex works to critical water infrastructure in the Toowoomba Region. Seymour Whyte, in alliance with SMEC and Toowoomba Regional Council, has been selected to help deliver this flagship project, bringing together construction delivery, engineering expertise and collaborative project leadership on one of Queensland’s most significant local government-led dam upgrades.
The scope includes spillway widening, dam crest raising, berm and spillway re-profiling, right-hand wall strengthening, plunge pool widening and deepening, flip bucket extension, instrumentation upgrades and associated enabling works. It is a rare opportunity to join Seymour Whyte on a technically challenging, high-profile project with major civil, structural, hydraulic and dam safety interfaces, and real long-term community impact.
We are seeking a Civil Site Engineer to join our project team. In this role, you will support the delivery of onsite engineering and construction activities, working closely with project teams to ensure works are delivered efficiently and in line with project requirements and quality standards.
Based on site in Biarra, this role offers a generous project uplift, attractive DIDO and LAFHA conditions, and the opportunity to contribute to a major, complex infrastructure project.
About the role:
- Coordinate and supervise civil construction activities to support efficient project delivery
- Monitor progress, quality and productivity, ensuring compliance with project specifications, ITPs and relevant standards
- Manage subcontractors, site documentation and reporting requirements
- Support cost control, planning and stakeholder coordination across the project
- Promote safety, quality and environmental compliance on site
We are looking for candidates who can demonstrate:
- Bachelor of Engineering (Civil)
- Demonstrated experience delivering civil infrastructure projects
- Knowledge of safety legislation, Australian Standards and industry codes
- Strong planning, monitoring and reporting capabilities to support effective project delivery
- Commitment to quality, safety and environmental practices.
We have a range of benefits available for our employees:
- Financial Wellbeing: competitive remuneration, salary continuance insurance and employee share program
- Generous Leave Benefits: purchased leave program, paid parental leave, and birthday leave – have your birthday off on us!
- Career Development: training, mentoring and leadership development programs
- Health & Wellness: discounted health insurance, seasonal vaccinations, fertility benefit and employee assistance program (EAP)
- Enjoy shopping, fitness and wellbeing discounts through our Flare and WHEREFIT partnerships including discounted gym memberships and classes
Seymour Whyte is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and we encourage applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds, including veterans.
Our commitment to an equitable construction industry extends to an inclusive culture that embraces our differences and gives everyone the opportunity to grow and be equally valued. We're unified in our direction toward having a workplace that is balanced and fair for all.
Next steps:
- Submit your CV online to apply for this role
- All successful applicants will be required to undergo a pre-employment medical and criminal history check
- Applications will only be accepted from candidates who have the right to work in Australia
To learn more about us, visit www.seymourwhyte.com.au
